Entries.Text: Navigation Editor
Navigation
This tool supports Elden Ring, Nightreign, The Duskbloods, Armored Core VI, Dark Souls III, Bloodborne and Sekiro.

Views, edits, generates and checks the navigation data of a loaded map: the navmeshes its characters path-find on, and how they connect. Start in the Overlay tab, which draws the navmesh in the viewport; the editing tabs work on what it draws. A new navmesh usually goes Models (Generate), then Stitch, then Gates, then Check.

How this works
The steps this tab is used in. Open the first time each tab is shown; the eye shows or hides it. The ? button above the tabs explains the terms.

1. Tick Show overlay above the tabs, and choose the n or o set.
2. Turn layers on or off: faces, edges, links, gates and ONAV. Each line layer shows its colour.
3. The other tabs edit what the overlay draws. The Map Editor's own navmesh drawing can be hidden with the Navmesh render filter.

1. Generate: select collision parts or assets in the viewport (with the map's collision loaded), tick Blocker on parts to go around, choose the target, and Generate.
2. Or Duplicate a model, moved by an offset, or Remove one, which leaves a placeholder.
3. Then select Stitch model to join the new model to its neighbours.
Each edit is one undo; saving the map writes the files.

Needs the overlay.
1. Choose the scope: the drawn set, the picked face's navmesh, or the selected model.
2. Find lists the broken connections and the new pairs. Nothing changes yet.
3. Apply makes the changes as one undo; with Update gates on, it rebuilds the gates of the changed pairs too.
Each set is stitched on its own: switch between n and o above the tabs and Find again.

Needs the overlay.
1. Tick Pick and move gates, then click a face or a gate marker to choose its navmesh.
2. Rebuild its gates after its connections change, or add, remove and drag gates by hand.
3. Recompute its costs after its vertices were moved.
Gates join the navmeshes of one map for the game's long-range path finding; they never cross maps.

Needs the overlay.
1. Tick Add links, and set Both ways and the edge data (Jump, Fall).
2. Click the face a link starts from, then the face it leads to.
3. Pick a face to see its links, block them or remove them.
In Dark Souls III, Bloodborne and Sekiro, links are user edge setups instead: a box at the ledge and one where it lands, on any navmesh.

Needs the overlay.
1. Tick Pick and click a face to see its data and edges, and type a new value.
2. Or tick Paint, choose Set, Add bits or Remove bits and a value (the bits, or a legend entry's Use), and drag over faces.
3. Each stroke is one undo. Face data changes no indices, so connections stay valid.

Needs the overlay.
1. Start Navmesh Edit and move the mouse over the drawn navmesh: the cursor shows the corner it moves.
2. Raise, lower or drag it with the keys under Controls. Radius moves the vertices around it too.
3. Commit Changes writes the moved vertices as one undo; Discard Changes puts them back. Until then they stay pending, on any tab.
After moving outer edges, stitch again; after large moves, recompute the gate costs.

1. Validate checks the map against the rules the game files follow, then compares the result with the vanilla files in the background.
2. New issues come from the project; inherited ones are in the vanilla files too.
3. Click an issue to go to its navmesh, face or gate.
Validate again after editing: the header says when the result is out of date.
Glossary
What the navigation terms the tabs use mean.
Navmesh

The surface characters path-find on: faces (polygons) joined by edges. A map's NVA file lists its navmeshes, one entry per model and set; the meshes themselves are Havok files in the map's nvmhktbnd binder.
n and o sets

Most games keep two navmeshes of each model: n, and o, most likely for larger characters, as its clearance reaches 5.1 m against n's 1.53 m. o usually has fewer faces. Each set has its own connections and links, and is edited on its own. Armored Core VI has the n set only.
NameID

The ID that connections, gates and node banks use for a navmesh. The game gives n entries NameIDs by a rule (from their place in the list or their model ID, depending on the game); an o entry repeats its n entry's NameID plus a fixed offset (2,000,000,000 in Elden Ring).
Placeholder
A navmesh entry without faces. A free placeholder, with no faces in either set and no gates, can take a generated or copied model; removing a model turns it into one.
Quarters (q files)

Some large Elden Ring navmeshes are split into four q files, and their n file is then empty. Quartered models can't be removed or copied, and a map that has them can't get new models; use a free placeholder there.
Connections (connectors, NVC)

Joins between boundary edges of two navmeshes, so a path can cross from one to the other: NVA connectors within a map, NVC files between neighbouring maps. A boundary edge with no connection is open. The Stitch tab finds and makes them.
Links (user edges)

Jumps, drops and ladders between two faces of one navmesh. Each is a pair of user edges, one on each face; a one-way link has its edge back blocked. The edge data gives the kind: 0x2 jump, 0x4 fall, 0x10 extra cost.
Gate nodes

Points where two navmeshes of a map meet, at most 16 per navmesh, each paired with a gate on the other side. The game's long-range path finding goes from gate to gate, using the walking cost stored between each two gates of a navmesh.
Clearance
How wide a character can be to pass, cached per edge and vertex in the navmesh file. Edits work it out again around what they change.
Face data

A 32-bit value per face that path finding reads: impassable, high cost, lava, ladder, gated (opened at runtime, as by a door), and others. The Face Data tab names the known bits and colours the faces by value.
Node banks
Lists of navmesh faces in the NVA, some with an entity ID. In Elden Ring, EMEVD 2003[13] turns the impassable bit of a bank's faces on or off, to block a path until an event flag is set.
ONAV
A per-map file of areas on a grid, with links between them (Elden Ring and Nightreign). The overlay draws it and Check checks it; the tool doesn't edit it.

Overlay
What the overlay shows. It is drawn slightly above the navmesh, and can't be selected.
Show overlay

Draws the overlay of the map picked above. Reading a map's navmesh files the first time can take a moment. The Map Editor's own navmesh drawing can be hidden with the Navmesh render filter, which doesn't hide the overlay.
n set
The n navmeshes (n files, and the q files they are split into), the first half of the NVA's entries: the ground for normal-sized characters.
o set

The o navmeshes (o files), the second half of the NVA's entries: the same ground as n, most likely for larger characters, as their clearance values reach 5.1 m against n's 1.53 m. They usually have fewer faces.
Face opacity
How opaque the face fills are.
{0} user edges lead to a face that couldn't be found, and are drawn without an arc.
Layers
The parts of the overlay to draw, with the colour each is drawn in.
Faces
The faces, filled in a colour for each face data value. The legend below lists the values.
Inner edges
The edges between two faces of the same navmesh. Dense on large maps.
Open edges
Boundary edges that no connection joins to another navmesh.
Connected in the map
Boundary edges an NVA connector joins to another navmesh of this map.
Connected to a neighbour
Boundary edges an NVC file joins to a navmesh of a neighbouring map.
User edges
Jump, ladder and drop links: the edge, and an arc to the face it leads to.
Blocked user edges
User edges that also carry the blocked flag.
Gate nodes
The NVA's gate nodes that pair with a gate of their neighbour, as see-through diamond markers. A gate and its partner share one point, so each has a short tick into its own navmesh.
Unpaired gate nodes
Gate nodes without a partner. The game's all point at a navmesh that already has 16 gates.
Broken gate nodes
Gate nodes whose target navmesh doesn't exist or isn't connected to them, or whose partner doesn't point back.
Gate costs
For the navmesh chosen in the Gates tab: a line between each two of its gates that can reach each other, labelled with the cost in metres.
ONAV areas
The ONAV's grid bounds, and a small box at each area's position.
ONAV links
Lines between the positions of linked ONAV areas.
ONAV cells
The grid cells each ONAV area covers. Heavy, and the order of the cell mask's bits is a guess: if the boxes don't line up with the areas, the guess is wrong.
Face Data
The face data values of the drawn faces, with the colour each is drawn in. Bits the game's navmesh code reads are named; the rest are listed by value only.

Change the face data of faces by dragging over them in the viewport. Each stroke is one undo. Face data changes no indices, so connections stay valid; the map's save writes the navmesh files.

Set

Add bits
Turn on the value's bits, keeping the faces' other bits.
Remove bits
Turn off the value's bits, keeping the faces' other bits.

The value to paint, in hexadecimal. The bits below, and the Use buttons of the legend, set it too. The bits list every bit the game's navmesh code reads, by name, and any other bit the drawn faces use.
A bit the drawn faces use. What it means in game is unknown.
Use
Paint this value.
The face's data in hexadecimal. Changing it is one undo.
Blocked
The user edge's blocked flag (EDGE_BLOCKED). Changing it is one undo.

The user edge's data in hexadecimal: 0x2 for a jump, 0x4 for a fall (with the drop in tenths of a metre in the high byte), and 0x10 for an extra cost, e.g. 0x204 or 0x314 in the game files. Changing it is one undo.
(unknown)
Impassable
No character can cross the face. In Elden Ring, EMEVD 2003[13] adds or removes this bit at runtime on the faces of a node bank, by its entity ID, to block a path until an event flag is set.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding (not in sealed worlds).
Checked
Part of the bits that make the game check a character before it crosses the face, but no rule for it alone was found.
Lava
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Lava navigation cross it, or, at an extra cost, characters in a state the game sets at runtime.
Ladder
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Ladder navigation cross it.
Opens 0x10000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x10000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x8000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x8000 is also set, which happens at runtime: a face that something in game opens, such as a door.
Huge enemy area
Costs more, by a world setting, for characters that avoid huge enemies (NpcThinkParam isNoAvoidHugeEnemy off).
Opens 0x100000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x100000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x80000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x80000 is also set, which happens at runtime.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding, on top of 0x8.
Character limit
Characters cross it only when a value of their physics (probably an angle) isn't above a limit stored in the navmesh. What the value is hasn't been identified. Only n faces use it.
Jump
A jump link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam enableJumpMove (enableJumpMove_onBattle in battle) allows it.
Fall
A drop link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam useFall_onNormalCaution (useFall_onSearchBattle in battle) allows it.
Extra cost
The link costs more: 4 for a jump, 2 for a fall.
Links

Add and remove links: jump, ladder and drop links between two faces of the same navmesh. A link is a pair of user edges, one on each face, as in the game's files. Each set (n and o) has its own links.
Add links in the viewport

While on, the first click on the drawn set picks the face a link starts from, and the second click the face it leads to, which adds the link. Turns picking and painting off, and turns itself off when you leave this tab.
Both ways
Characters can use the link in both directions. When off, the edge back is blocked (EDGE_BLOCKED), as in the game's one-way links such as drops.
The edge data both edges of a new link get (hex). The game's links use 2 for a jump, and values ending in 04 or 14 for a fall, whose higher bits vary.
Clearance

The clearance cache value of the new edges: how wide a character can use the link, as a fraction of the cache's ceiling (254 = the ceiling, 1.53 m in the n set and 5.1 m in the o set). The game's links use values such as 69, 102, 135 and 168.

Stitch

Re-stitch the connections of the drawn set: find the connections whose edges no longer fit, and the boundary edges of two navmeshes that lie along each other, within the map (NVA) and across its NVC files with loaded neighbours. Find shows what would change; Apply makes it, as one undo.

Drawn set
Look at the connections and edges of every navmesh of the drawn set.
Picked face's navmesh

Selected model
Only look at the connections and edges of the selected model's navmesh in the drawn set (n or o). Select the model in the Models tab; Stitch model after Generate or Duplicate selects it for you.
Select a model in the Models tab first, or choose another scope.
The selected model is split into quarters (q files): pick a face of the quarter to stitch and use the picked face's navmesh.
Model {0:D6} has no navmesh in the drawn set. Switch the set above the tabs.
Stitch model {0:D6}

Opens the Stitch tab on this model, with gates updated, and finds what joining it to its neighbours would change. Nothing changes until Apply. Stitch each set: switch to the other set above the tabs and Find again.
Include loaded neighbours
Also join edges across the NVC files of this map, with the neighbour maps that are loaded with their navmesh files. Only existing NVC files are used; none is made.
Only join open edges

Only join edges that have no connection yet, which changes the game's data least. When off, an edge that already has a connection can get another, as the game's partly overlapping edges do: this repairs more, but also adds pairs the game left apart.
Max separation
The largest distance across, seen from above, between two edges that are joined. Half the game's connections are 0; 90% are under 2.3 cm.
Max step height
The largest height difference between two joined edges where they overlap. 99% of the game's in-map connections are under 0.46 m.
Min overlap
The shortest length two edges must overlap by to be joined.
Find
Finds what a re-stitch of the drawn set would change, without changing anything.

Generate

Generate a model's n and o navmeshes from the collision parts and assets selected in the viewport, with Recast. Each part's collision is used where the part is placed. The result is a starting point: it covers the walkable surfaces of what is selected, including places the game's navmeshes leave out (roofs, ledges).
The map's collision isn't loaded. Turn on collision loading in the Map Editor's settings and load the map again.
Selected parts

What the generation reads, from the viewport selection: each collision part's high collision, and each asset's own collision (high, else low), placed where the part is. Select more parts (in any loaded map) to include them.
{0} collision parts and {1} assets selected. Tick Blocker on a part to generate around it instead of on it.
Replace model {0:D6}'s navmesh
The generated meshes replace the selected model's n and o files. Its connections and node bank faces name the old faces, so they are dropped: re-stitch it afterwards. Its gate nodes are kept.
Into a free placeholder
The generated meshes go into a placeholder with no faces, as a new model.
Give it the collision model's ID
The placeholder takes the ID of the first chosen collision model, as the game's models have their collision's ID, if no other model has it. Its NameIDs don't change.
The map has no target for the edit: no model to replace, no free placeholder, and models can't be added to it.
n set
o set
The voxel and character settings this set is generated with. The defaults are tuned against the game's navmeshes.
Cell size
The horizontal size of a voxel. Smaller follows the collision more closely, and takes longer.
Agent radius
How far the navmesh is kept from walls and ledges. It is rounded up to whole voxels.
Agent height
The headroom a character needs. Lower ceilings are left out.
Max climb
The highest step a character climbs.
Max slope
The steepest slope a character walks up.
Max edge length
The longest a boundary edge may be; 0 for no limit.
Face size
Face size: off (Recast's faces)

Splits every face along a world grid of this size, so the faces are even (links and face data are set per face): none is wider than the size across X or Z. The grid lines sit at whole multiples of the size, so neighbouring models split their shared borders alike. 0 keeps Recast's faces, which can be several metres across. Coverage doesn't change.
Spill
Spill: off

Lets the navmesh reach this far out past a ledge of its collision, level with the ledge. Recast keeps the mesh an agent radius in from every edge; the spill moves the boundary vertices at a drop out to the ledge and then past it, so the faces either side of a jump or fall come close, as the game's AI needs to use the link (ER, NR). Vertices against a wall, or where the way out meets the collision or a blocker, stay where they are, and blockers still cut the spilled faces. 0 for none.
Triangles only
Splits every face into triangles, after the grid. A corner on a straight edge, shared with a neighbour, is kept, so a few faces may have four corners.
Jump and fall links

Adds links between faces from the height change across each ledge and gap. From every boundary edge, about every metre, the first surface outward within the reach is linked: within the jump height either way as a jump, both ways (edge data 0x2); lower than that, down to the fall height, as a fall, one way (0x4, with the drop in tenths of a metre in the high byte, as the game's are). None where the path through the air meets collision or a blocker, or where the faces are already a short walk apart.

Jump height: off (falls only)
Ends that differ in height by up to this, either way, are joined by a jump that goes both ways. The game's n jumps are mostly within 2.6 m. 0 makes falls only, as the game's o meshes have.
Fall height
The deepest drop a fall link goes down. Drops deeper than the jump height and the climb are falls, one way. The game's falls go down by up to about 15 m.
Link reach
How far out from a ledge or gap the landing is looked for, across. The game's links reach up to 5 m in n and 9 m in o.

Edit

Moves navmesh vertices in the viewport. The cursor sits on the drawn navmesh set (Overlay tab), and the nearest corner of the face under it can be raised, lowered or dragged. Faces, edges and connections are kept; on commit the navmesh's bounds, face tree and clearance values around the moved vertices are worked out again. Moving a map's outer edges can part them from a neighbouring map's navmesh: re-stitch (Stitch tab) or keep them in place.
Tick Show overlay above the tabs to edit: the cursor works on the navmesh set it draws.
Actions
Start or stop editing, and commit or discard the edits.
Start Navmesh Edit

Shows the cursor on the navmesh under the mouse, so its vertices can be moved with the keys below. Turns off picking, painting and linking. Stops when you leave this tab; edits that aren't committed are kept.
Stop Navmesh Edit
Hides the cursor. Edits that haven't been committed are kept, and can be committed or discarded later.
Commit Changes
Puts the moved vertices in the edited navmesh files, with their bounds, face trees and nearby clearance values worked out again. Can be undone; saving the map writes the navmesh binder.
Discard Changes
Puts every moved vertex back where it was.

Gates

The gate nodes of the drawn set: the points where two navmeshes of the map meet, which the game's high-level path graph runs through, with the walking cost between each two gates of a navmesh. Gate nodes never cross maps.

Pick and move gates in the viewport

A click on a gate's marker chooses it and its navmesh; a click on a face chooses that face's navmesh. Click the chosen gate again and drag to move it: it slides along its navmesh's connection edges to its target, its partner moves with it, and the costs are walked again on release. Clicks don't select map objects meanwhile. Turns itself off when you leave this tab.
